newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria cancels local air fare rise by airlines.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria cancels local air fare rise by airlines.

text.p: Nigeria's aviation ministry on Friday cancelled a 200 percent increase in local air fares announced by airline operators.
The Nigerian Airline Operators (AON) said on Thursday it would raise the fares by 200 percent from Monday.
"The purported hike in domestic air fares by the airlines is illegal and of no effect," said aviation ministry spokesman John Edem in a statement.
"Only the aviation minister has the statutory authority to announce changes in air fares," he added.
Elijah Omokhodion, chairman of AON, had said on Thursday that the decision to jack up the fares was the only way to keep the airline industry healthy.

It would have meant an economy one-way ticket to the capital Abuja from Lagos, a distance of about 800 km, (500 miles) would cost 7,920 naira ($99), three times more than the current price of 2,685 naira ($33.56).
Edem's statement said: "The aviation minister met with the AON's representatives last week and made recommendations to the National Utility Commission. There has been no final word."
Government would punish any airline operator that implemented the new fare from Monday, it said.
The airlines have long campaigned for an increase in domestic airfares, saying this would help sustain their operations in an economy that has been in recession for years.
In November, the military government cancelled what it called an "insensitive" 100 percent increase in domestic air fares annnounced by AON.
Government announced in this year's budget in January that airline operators would no longer pay tariffs on aircraft spare parts.
AON welcomed the concession but said it was only with the 200 percent increase that airlines could earn enough to keep aircraft in good condition and maintain high safety standards.
A spate of air accidents in Nigeria since last year, blamed by aviation experts on a tight squeeze in the industry, has given the travelling public much cause for worry.
